findings.text: claim (a) holds — an aliased constant escapes the audit: the reference filter runs before the anchoring check, so `expected = router.LaneCapacity.OCCUPANCY_TARGET` then `assert produced == expected` yields 0 findings where the unaliased spelling yields 1 (logs/experiments.log A0 vs A1). That is the exact circular shape section 1 describes.

claim (b) holds — _bound_literals unions literal bindings across every scope of the file, so a sound pin in one test function anchors a same-named chain in another (logs/experiments.log B0 vs B1 differ only in the local variable's name).

claim (c) fails for literal operands, holds for module-bound literal names — 0 of the 135 carries an operand with a module-bound literal name and 0 conveys a guard-anchored operand, but `_is_literal` does not see written-out data behind a constructor, so three chains that already pin their value are reported: tests/camdyn/test_conditioning.py:57 and tests/camdyn/test_field_leakage_guard.py:30 (frozenset({'efm', 'esm', 'xdc'}) == BANNED_CONDITIONING_SOURCES), and tests/spine_bench/test_parity.py:371 (pytest.approx(0.001245365781787239) == parity.MIGRATION_SEAM_RESIDUAL_BUDGET) - see logs/predicates.log.

the audit aborts on the first unparsable module, so under an interpreter below the project's 3.14 the run exits 2 with no findings at all rather than scanning the rest; the repository already carries that class of module (tests/test_agent_router_gate:404); reproduce in logs/abort-under-3.11.log.
